| 2026-10-27 | PL2-D-65   | `[OWNER]` **OWNER-QUESTIONS #6 answered.** (1) Duplicates after an unknown outcome are not acceptable for every message. PL3 NOTIFY gives every message type a resend class: _safe to resend_ (OTPs, login and security alerts, receipts) is resent once after an unknown outcome, and delivery reports remove the duplicate where the vendor provides one; _hold for review_ (collection or recovery reminders, legal and demand notices, KFS and loan-term communications, anything that could read as harassment or a second legal notice) is never resent automatically after an unknown outcome and is queued for a person to confirm. An unclassified type defaults to hold for review. Until PL3 the adapters keep the PL2-D-64 behaviour, which is acceptable because nothing is sent for real. (2) The Gupshup URL secret is accepted as interim, on conditions now built: the `ipb_token` must be at least 32 random bytes (43 base64url characters; shorter is refused) and is rotated like other webhook secrets (C-19); the telemetry scrubber redacts credential-named query parameters (`ipb_token`, `*token`, `*secret`, `api_key`, `key`, `sig`, `signature`, `password`) from every log, span and error attribute; the source-IP allow-list applies as soon as Gupshup publishes ranges; and a state-changing event is passed on only after its status is confirmed. Gupshup documents no status-lookup API yet [VERIFY in the sandbox], so `confirmStatus` is injected and without it Gupshup events are acknowledged but withheld. Revisit once the vendor test accounts exist; both Gupshup adapters stay unproven until then. (3) Brevo is used for sending only: no contact records and no manual blocks (OWN-15); the PL3 NOTIFY suppression list is the single source of truth File contents are otherwise identical. Tarballs are therefore reproducible in content, not byte for byte; the registry values are the reference, and `registry-dist.yml` (manual) gains a `compare_ref` mode that rebuilds at a commit and diffs each tarball against the registry's. | 2026-10-29 | R1-D-25 | **Database-level statutory audit capture as built (Finbyx PR-FBX-10 item 2, owner request 29 Oct 2026; R1-plan M17).** (1) **Scope:** tables a product registers with`audit.register_capture`(books of account, for the Companies (Accounts) Rules 2014 r.3(1) edit log). Every insert, update and delete is captured with before and after values, the application actor, entity, branch, break-glass grant, trace, action and reason, the database login and role, the transaction id and the time. (2) **Writer:**`audit.capture_row()`, SECURITY DEFINER, owned by `capture_writer`. No application, read-only, migration or support role holds that role (the read-only-role check covers it), and the update, delete and truncate refusals are enabled always. (3) **Chain:** per tenant, SHA-256 as the ledger's (PL1-C-01, no new cryptography). The canonical form is a sorted JSON object of charset-restricted fields, with values, row key and reason as SHA-256 digests of their stored text, so TypeScript re-computes it from the rows alone. (4) **Anchor:** the daily anchor's format 2 signs the day's capture head with the ledger head (KMS, as before). Format 1 stays for tenants with nothing captured, and `verifyCaptureAgainstAnchor`checks an export against it. (5) **Cannot be disabled:** no flag or setting;`ddl_command_end`and`sql_drop`event triggers refuse what would remove or disable any part;`register_capture`refuses until the guard is installed (event triggers need the database owner's privilege, on a managed service its administrative role); triggers are enabled ALWAYS against replica mode. (6) **Gap detector:**`AuditService.verifyCapture`(daily through`AuditSweep.verifyCaptureAll`) checks the chain, the head and `audit.capture_problems()`, including a disabled guard. A break is ledgered (`audit.capture.break_detected`) and raises `LedgerChainBroken`with an`entry_id`of`capture:<seq>`. (7) **Kernel:** `MutateOptions.reason`(1 to 500 characters); the kernel sets`app.action`and`app.reason`with the other transaction settings. A setting that does not fit its column is recorded as absent, so it never blocks a write. (8) **Retention:** capture rows are kept as the ledger is (IPB-02-52, eight years, never deleted by the platform). No new retention rule. (9) **Residual:** a superuser who disables the event triggers can then disable a refusal. The chain shows the change, the verification reports the disabled guard, and PostgreSQL logs the DDL | IPB-02-51, IPB-02-52, §02.4.7.1; PL1-C-01 |
| 2026-10-29 | R1-D-26 | **Branch context as built (Finbyx PR-FBX-10 item 1, owner request 29 Oct 2026; R1-plan M18).** (1) **Context:**`KernelContext.branchId`(the branch a change is made in),`branchIds`(the branches whose rows the principal may see, at most 1000) and`allBranches`(every branch, e.g. head office). Ids are`[A-Za-z0-9*.:-]{1,64}`, so a comma can never split one into two. A `branchId`outside`branchIds`is refused with IPB-SEC-005 unless`allBranches`is set. (3) **RLS:** products add`tenancy.branch_allowed(branch_id)` to a table's policy beside the tenant condition (`tenancy/0007`). It denies by default: no branch context, an unlisted branch and a row without a branch are refused, except under `all`. The tenant condition stays the isolation boundary; the branch narrows within it. (4) **Ledger:** `audit.ledger.branch_id` (`audit/0004`). The chain hashes it only when it is set, so every earlier entry, and every entry without a branch, hashes exactly as before (`canonicalEntry`adds the key only when present). | 2026-10-29 | R1-D-27 | **Inbound idempotency as built (Finbyx PR-FBX-10 item 4; IPB-10-07, §10.4; R1-plan M20).** (1) **Store:**`tenancy.idempotency_key` (`tenancy/0008`) with IPB-10 §10.4's columns. It lives in the tenancy schema, which owns the request context, rather than an `api`schema: a naming deviation only. It has forced RLS by tenant and a unique key per tenant, and the response body is classed REGULATED. (2) **Claim in the change's transaction:**`idempotent(tx, request, work, { audit })`runs`work`once per key. The key row commits with the change, so there is no`in_progress` row to leave behind, and a failed request stores nothing and may be retried. An identical replay within the TTL returns the stored status and body (`Idempotent-Replayed`, `Idempotent-Original-Request-Id`) and writes an `api.idempotency.replay`ledger entry. Another route or body under the key is 409 IPB-PORT-004; a key whose first request is still running is 409 IPB-API-011 (a transaction advisory lock). (3) **Edge:**`IdempotencyKeyInterceptor` (`@infrabyx/tenancy/nest`) requires a UUIDv7 `Idempotency-Key`on POST and PATCH (400 IPB-API-010), puts the key, route and canonical request hash on the request, and maps the result to the response. (4) **Expiry:**`int.api.idempotency_ttl_hours`(24, never below 24, at most 168);`IdempotencyExpiry`deletes expired keys per tenant through`TenantSweep`, with a restrictive policy so only expired keys can be deleted. | 2026-10-29 | R1-D-34 | **V-CIP design against the RBI (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/361, updated 29 Dec 2025; the copy uploaded to Finbyx PR #9), for owner answer #90 (b).** What the design must meet, by clause, and where it lands (built in the next session; nothing is built here): (1) **Para 5(2)(xiv) and para 27(2)(i):** an authorised official of the NBFC, specially trained, conducts the call and does the liveness check; the platform's V-CIP session has a named official participant, refuses to complete without one, and Digio's liveness and face-match scores are shown to the official as support only (para 27(1)(v): "ultimate responsibility … rests with the NBFC"; para 27(1)(vi) allows AI). (2) **Para 27(1)(i):** infrastructure on the NBFC's premises or its cloud with data ownership resting with it, the connection originating from its own secured network domain, all data and the recording moved to its own servers immediately after the call, and the cloud provider or third-party technology provider retaining nothing. LiveKit runs in the tenant's (the NBFC's) deployment, recordings go straight to the tenant's STORAGE target, and frames reach Digio only by a short-lived reference, with no-retention as a contract term the owner must get from Digio and the host (owner task). (3) **Para 27(1)(ii):** end-to-end encryption between the customer device and the hosting point (LiveKit with TLS and SRTP; end-to-end encryption to be assessed against server-side recording) and consent recorded in an auditable, alteration-proof way (the`consent`receipt and the ledger). (4) **Para 27(1)(iii):** connections from outside India or from spoofed IPs refused (an India-only check at the room join). (5) **Para 27(1)(iv):** the recording carries live GPS coordinates and date and time stamps (captured from the device and burned into the recording's metadata); video quality adequate to identify the customer. (6) **Para 27(1)(vii) to (ix):** forged-identity cases reported as cyber events; VA, penetration test and security audit by CERT-In-empanelled auditors before rollout and periodically, and functional and performance testing (owner tasks before go-live). (7) **Para 27(2)(ii) to (iv):** a pause or reconnect must not create several video files, a dropped call starts a fresh session; the question sequence varies; prompting at the customer end rejects the session. (8) **Para 27(2)(vi) to (ix) and (xi) to (xiii):** audio, video and a photograph captured; identification by Aadhaar OTP e-KYC, offline Aadhaar, CKYCR or DigiLocker; the Aadhaar number redacted (para 23); offline XML or QR not older than three working days, and the video step within three working days of fetching the identity; a PAN image captured and verified with the issuer; the official confirms the photo match. (9) **Para 27(2)(xiv):** accounts opened through V-CIP stay non-operational until a concurrent audit (Finbyx's workflow). (10) **Para 27(3):** all V-CIP data and recordings stored in India, time-stamped and searchable, under the record-management rules (para 47: at least five years after the relationship ends); the activity log kept with the official's credentials (the ledger). (11) **Para 44(1):** where V-CIP is offered it is the first option for remote onboarding (Finbyx's journey). Items (2), (6), (9) and (11) need the owner or Finbyx; the rest is platform adapter and room work | RBI KYC Directions 2025 paras 5(2)(xiv), 23, 26, 27, 44, 47; owner answer #90 |

| 2026-11-03 | R1-D-58 | **Chain lanes for the ledger and the statutory capture (Finbyx PR-FBX-32, pilot-critical; ADR-0005).** Both chains locked one head row per tenant on every append, so a tenant's writing transactions ran one at a time: Finbyx's COB measured about 22 loans a second whatever the number of workers, about 158,000 loans in the 2-hour window against the 1,000,000 required. Each tenant now has 32 lanes per chain (`audit.lane_setting`, raised only). A transaction takes the first lane it can lock without waiting (its preferred lane `hash(txid) mod N` first) and keeps it until it ends; each lane is today's SHA-256 chain (PL1-C-01) with `lane` and `lane_seq` hashed. `seq` becomes a global sequence (unique, increasing in each lane, with gaps). Existing chains continue as lane 0 from each tenant's old head, which its first append after the upgrade reads `FOR UPDATE`, so no backfill runs in the migration (`no-data-in-ddl`) and nothing written changes. Lane heads are written only by the chain owners; the verifiers compare each lane's end with its head, so a deleted tail is reported (new for the ledger). The daily anchor (format 3) signs every lane head of both chains: the cross-lane seal. No new cryptography and no IPB-02 control weakened: every append is still chained in its transaction, and every change to history still breaks a chain or an anchor. Rejected: chaining after the fact by a job (entries unchained in between), and one append per transaction (the head is still held to commit). Measured (4 vCPU, PostgreSQL 16, two captured rows and one ledger entry per transaction): 16 writers 314 tx/s on one lane against 1,027 tx/s with lanes; with transactions held 20 ms, 39 tx/s against 360 tx/s; one writer 281 against 303. Migrations `audit/0006`, `audit/0007` (concurrent indexes); `audit` minor. The export-map gate required `REF-EXPORT-1.4`: `audit_event` gains `lane` and `lane_seq`, `verify.mjs` checks lane by lane after reading every month, golden archives normalise the run-time `seq` and lane (`export` minor; 1.3 stays for the dual run). | 2026-11-04 | R1-D-92 | **Security patch: no work on a connection after its transaction ended (`tenancy` patch).** Reproduced with a one-connection pool: a joined call still running when its ambient mutation ended (a sibling of a refused concurrent call) ran its next statement in the next transaction on the returned connection, another tenant's (`app.tenant_id` read `tnt_b`). Fix: `PgTx` is marked ended before commit or rollback and refuses every later statement, unit or settings change (`KernelGuardError`); `JoinedTx` ends with its unit; an ambient mutation tracks its joined calls, waits for those still running before it ends and then fails (it never commits half a call), and refuses a joined call that starts after it ended. Released as a patch through one CI gate; every product upgrades before its next exit gate (adoption notes). Product exposure: Finbyx's code (searchable) does not call `kernel.ambient`; Udofin (which asked for it, PR-UDF-033) and LawDocsComply could not be searched from here, and no product logs are reachable. | IPB-02-12 (tenant isolation); IPB-02 §02.4.2; R1-D-48 |

| 2026-11-17 | R1-D-167 | **R1-D-166 fixed: the Zitadel customer adapter confirms every search hit with `GET /v2/users/{id}`.** Research (zitadel/zitadel at tag v4.19.5, read 17 Nov 2026): `GetUserByID` in `internal/api/grpc/user/v2/user_query.go` calls `GetUserByIDWithPermission(ctx, true, ...)`, and with `true` `internal/query/user.go` first runs `triggerUserProjections` (the user and login-name projections, `handler.WithAwaitRunning()` in `internal/query/query.go`), so it reads the account's latest events; `ListUsers` (`POST /v2/users`) calls `SearchUsers`, which reads the projection as it is. That is the lag `pnpm check:full` hit. **Fix (`connectors` patch):** a private `holds(userId, username)` reads the account by id and answers `holds` only when its id and current username match and its state is not `USER_STATE_INACTIVE` or `USER_STATE_DELETED` (`zitadel.user.v2.UserState`, `proto/zitadel/user/v2/user.proto`; a locked or initial account still holds its login, and Zitadel refuses its sessions itself); `userByName` returns a search hit only when `holds` confirms it; `resolveUser` returns the account at the login's own candidate id when it holds the login (an account the search has not indexed yet, which the old code skipped and then failed to re-create), skips a candidate that is retired or moved, and after a refused create first checks the id it tried; `idpFindUser` also walks the candidate ids, stopping at the first that does not exist (the platform never deletes an account; a hand-deleted one can only make it miss, and Zitadel's unique usernames still refuse a second holder); any other status from `GET` fails the call (`IPB-IDN-002` on a 5xx, `IPB-PORT-001`/`002` otherwise) instead of creating on a guess. Optional `fetchImpl` added to the options, as on `ZitadelIdentity`. **Tests:** `zitadel-customer.test.ts` (4 cases, a fake Zitadel whose search answers from a snapshot): a just-retired login gets a new account and the code is issued for it; a moved login is not found on the old number; an unindexed account is found, not created twice; an unconfirmable hit is refused; all four fail on the old adapter. The Zitadel leg gets a contract case that pins the login's search to its pre-retirement answer through a proxy, so the real instance's `GET` decides on every run rather than only under load. Keycloak (`byLogin` reads its database) is unaffected. **[VERIFY]** Zitadel logs a failed projection trigger at debug level and reads anyway, and no Zitadel document states read-your-writes for `GetUserByID` as a contract; recorded as a residual in threat model §3.53. | PR-UDF-034; IPB-02-01; R1-D-166; R1-D-51 |

| 2026-11-19 | R1-D-198 | **PR-UDF-045 built: the RE-hosted V-CIP launcher, its signed hand-off, `vcipStatus` by call, reason codes and the liveness mode.** (1) **Launcher:** `KycPort.launchVcip?({ context, jws }, call) → VcipLaunch` (`vcipId`, `launchUrl`, `expiresAt` and the evidence), optional on the interface so an implementer outside the platform does not break in a minor (as R1-D-193's `startDigilocker`), beside `startVcip`, which needs an official and a VIDEO_MEET room and so belongs to the RE's conductor; the LSP hosts no V-CIP component (KYC Directions 2025 para 27(1)(i)). (2) **Hand-off:** `VcipHandoffContext` in `contracts`: `tenantId`, `reId`, `lspId`, `customerRef`, `journeyId` (ids: letters, digits and `. _ : -`, 3 to 200), `issuedAt`, `expiresAt` (ISO 8601), `nonce` (22 to 64 base64url); strict; every field classed (INTERNAL, the customer reference and journey CONFIDENTIAL); at most 900 s (`VCIP_HANDOFF_MAX_LIFETIME_SECONDS`) from issue to expiry and expiring after its issue; a field holding a 12-digit run or an Aadhaar-like number (`findAadhaarLike`) is refused. The LSP signs the context with the existing `signRegulatedMessage` (the context as the signed object; ES256, `kid`, `jti`, `iat`; owner answer #82, G5) and the adapter verifies it with the existing `verifyRegulatedMessage` and a `ReplayStore`: **no new algorithm, key type or primitive**, and no migration (the replay store is the product's, as for DPoP and Digio's consents). Because the JWS is detached, the signature is over the context presented, so "the verified payload equals the context" holds by construction: a JWS over another context fails its signature. The JWS's `iat` window (five minutes by default) also applies, so an LSP signs right before it hands over. (3) **Order and refusals:** parse; the call's tenant (when given), the adapter's RE and a trusted LSP (a key ring per `lspId`, so an LSP's key vouches only for itself); the signature with the replay claim (only a verified message burns its `jti`); then the context's times (`vcipHandoffTimeRefusal`: issued at most 60 s ahead, not expired); all before any vendor call or stored row. Each refusal is `IPB-PORT-001`, definite, with one of `VCIP_HANDOFF_REFUSALS`: `handoff_invalid` (malformed, overlong, other tenant or RE, untrusted LSP or key, tampered, a JWS over another context, an `iat` ahead), `handoff_replayed` (`jti` seen), `handoff_expired` (the context expired or the JWS stale); `vcipHandoffFailure` maps the JWS failures. The answer's `launchUrl` passes `vcipLaunchUrlAllowed` (the DigiLocker return-address check of R1-D-193, `https:`, exact hosts, no user information, no 12-digit run, plus `findAadhaarLike`), else `IPB-PORT-003` `launch_url_invalid`; `expiresAt` is the hand-off's. A hand-off is single use; a lost answer is retried with a freshly signed hand-off, and the unclaimed session lapses. (4) **Which implementers:** no vendor adapter in the platform offers an RE-hosted launcher, so `DigioKyc` and `IdfyKyc` refuse `launchVcip` `unsupported` (`[VERIFY]` whether either offers one); `VcipConductor`, the RE's side of the call, is the one that takes hand-offs (`handoff: { reId, issuers, replay, launchBaseUrl, launchHosts? }`, the base checked when it is built): it stores a `scheduled` session (`sessionId` the journey id, `officialRef` and `roomId` empty, `launchExpiresAt`), answers `launchBaseUrl` plus the session id, and the RE's official starts it with `startVcip({ …, vcipId })` (`VcipSession.vcipId`, optional), for the hand-off's tenant and customer only (`customer_mismatch`), while it is live (`launch_expired`); a scheduled session reads `expired` with `reasonCode: "launch_expired"` once its hand-off lapses. Without `handoff` the conductor refuses `not_configured`. `FakeKyc` implements the launcher with a `LocalKms` development key (`FAKE_VCIP_HANDOFF`, `signFakeVcipHandoff`, `fakeVcipHandoffKeys`, `fakeVcipHandoffContext`). `kycMethodRouter` routes `launchVcip` under `vcip` and never moves it past an unavailable adapter (the hand-off is single use and the first may have scheduled a session). (5) **`vcipStatus(vcipId, call?)`:** an optional `PortCall`, so no caller breaks; the fake and the conductor read under `call.tenantId` (another tenant's session is `not_found`); the conductor still takes a tenant string as before. `PortCall` has no trace field; the trace stays in the tenancy context. (6) **Reason codes:** `VcipManifest.reason` was a free string, so retyping it would break an implementer that sets it and a reader that compares it with a literal; instead `reasonCode?: VcipReasonCode` (`VCIP_REASON_CODES`: `official_rejected`, `liveness_failed`, `face_mismatch`, `document_mismatch`, `outside_india`, `customer_declined`, `customer_left`, `connection_lost`, `official_unavailable`, `launch_expired`, `other`) is added and the free `reason` is kept, `@deprecated`, never to be shown (the plan's `reasonText` is that same field under its old name). | 2026-11-19 | R1-D-199 | **PR-UDF-046 built: webhook verification without a vendor call (`KycPort.verifyWebhook`; Standard Webhooks under C-13).** (1) **Method:** `KycPort.verifyWebhook?(rawBody, headers, meta?) → KycWebhookReceipt` (`eventId`, the `webhook-id`; `vcipId`; `receivedAt`, by the adapter's clock), optional on the interface so an implementer outside the platform does not break in a minor (as R1-D-198's `launchVcip`): size, signature, window and replay only, with no vendor call and no read-back, so a product answers 401 to an unverified event, records `eventId` in its module inbox (`PgInbox.firstSeen`), acknowledges within 2 s and reads the session back with `vcipStatus` from QUEUE_PORT (IPB-10-27). `handleWebhook` keeps its signature; where `verifyWebhook` exists it is `verifyWebhook` and then `vcipStatus`. Each refusal is `IPB-API-018` (401, as every inbound webhook verifier since PL2-D-64) with a `KYC_WEBHOOK_REFUSALS` label (`body_too_large`, `signature_invalid`, `timestamp_stale`, `event_replayed`), definite, never carrying the body (`kycWebhookRefused`); a verified body that names no well-formed session (letters, digits and `. _ : -`, 3 to 200, no 12-digit run or Aadhaar-like number) is `IPB-PORT-001` `malformed_event`. Only a verified delivery is claimed, so a forgery cannot burn a real id. The replay key is the delivery's id **and** timestamp: a provider's retry of one event (the same `webhook-id` with a new timestamp and signature) verifies again and the inbox de-duplicates it by `eventId`, while a captured delivery sent again is `event_replayed`; a key on the id alone would turn a lost acknowledgement into a lost event. Verification only; `signStandardWebhookForTest` signs for tests and the hermetic leg, as `signLiveKitWebhookForTest` does. No new algorithm, key type or primitive; the specification's own example is a test vector, and the registry's C-13 line names the scheme. **RFC 9421 is not built:** no verifier exists, and one (a signature base over covered components, with its algorithms) is new cryptography, so it waits for the owner (#150). (4) **Which implementers:** `FakeKyc` verifies Standard Webhooks with `FAKE_KYC_WEBHOOK.secret` (derived from a fixed label; it protects nothing) or `webhook: { secrets, replay }`, counts read-backs (`vcipStatusVendorCalls`) and its `handleWebhook` now refuses an unsigned event (`signFakeKycWebhook` signs one). `DigioKyc` and `IdfyKyc` refuse `verifyWebhook` `unsupported` and keep `handleWebhook` `unsupported`: neither vendor's V-CIP webhook scheme is documented in this repository (the Digio eSign adapter records that Digio documents no webhook signature) `[VERIFY]`. `standardWebhookKycVerifier({ adapter, secrets, replay, vcipIdOf, now? })` in `@infrabyx/connectors/kyc` builds the `verifyWebhook` of an adapter whose provider signs with Standard Webhooks (the secrets read from SECRETS on each delivery, after the size check). `VcipConductor` takes no provider webhooks (its sessions move by the official's calls), so nothing is wired there. `kycMethodRouter` routes `verifyWebhook` under `vcip`; an `IPB-API-018` is final and an adapter without the method is passed over. (5) **Tests:** two contract cases (a signed event answers ids only with no vendor call, a provider's retry verifies and `handleWebhook` reads back; eight forged, tampered, unsigned, stale, future, replayed or oversize deliveries refused with their label by both methods with no vendor call, and a signed empty body `malformed_event`) run on the fake and as `unsupported` on the Digio and IDfy stubs, with a `findAadhaarLike` sweep of the receipt and the refusals; unit tests cover the order and labels (`contracts`), the verifier (`crypto`: the specification's example, rotation, `v1a`, the window, malformed headers, bad secrets), the connectors verifier and the router. **`[ASSUMED – owner review]` (#150):** Standard Webhooks verification read as C-13; RFC 9421 left for the owner; the replay key; four labels, a missing header counted as `signature_invalid`; the fake's `handleWebhook` refusing unsigned events in a minor; Digio and IDfy `unsupported`. | PR-UDF-046 (R1-D-180); C-13, C-19, PL2-D-48, PL2-D-64; IPB-10-21, IPB-10-24, IPB-10-27; R1-D-198; plan §J |

| 2026-11-20 | R1-D-234 | **The intermittent CI-only `integration` failure (version PR #326, run 44694342487 attempt 1) found and fixed, with no retry (owner, 20 Nov 18:50).** The job log, readable this time through the GitHub job-log tool, names `notify` `src/__tests__/staff.int.test.ts` "sends once per idempotency key": the replay answered `[A2, A1]` where the first call answered `[A1, A2]`. Cause: the first call answers `staffHolders` (ordered by user id), the replay rebuilds the list from `notify.delivery` `order by created_at, id`, and delivery ids are ULIDs whose 80-bit random part is not monotonic within one millisecond (`@infrabyx/crypto` `ulid`), so rows written in the same millisecond come back in random order. The receipt (`deliveryReceipt`) had the same latent order. Fix (`notify` and `contracts` patches): `StaffSendResult.recipients` and `DeliveryReceipt.recipients` are sorted by principal id in code-point order on every path, and the port comments say so. Test: a new case freezes `Date` so every delivery shares one millisecond and checks the order on eight first calls, replays and receipts; it fails on the old code (run locally) and passed three runs in a row with the fix. Other `order by created_at, id` reads in `notify` return deliveries whose order no test or caller relies on; left as they are. |

| 2026-11-20 | R1-D-237 | `[ASSUMED – owner review]` **Udofin PR-UDF-062 built: `PgKernel.ambient` joins another principal of the tenant, runs another tenant's call on its own and queues concurrent joined calls (threat model §3.161).** (1) **Another principal of the tenant:** a `mutate` inside `ambient` by a different principal, with the ambient call's tenant and scope and the app role, joins in a kernel savepoint with its own `app.*` settings (actor, entity, action, reason, branches, trace), so RLS and the ledger's insert policy (`actor_id = app.actor_id`) see that principal and its ledger entries name it (its `tx.ctx` is its own context). After it, the settings of the call it was made from (the ambient call's, or an outer joined call's for a nested one) are put back on every path (released, rolled back or refused) before any other call may use the connection. With `joinReads` its `read`s join the same way (read role, read-only, a savepoint that is always rolled back; R1-D-188). The same principal keeps R1-D-48's rule (the same break-glass grant). Nested calls now get their outer joined call's settings back, not the ambient call's. (2) **Another tenant:** never joined. A `mutate` or `read` for another tenant runs under `AsyncLocalStorage.exit`, in its own transaction on another pool connection, as if no ambient mutation were open (a call nested in it does not join either), so neither tenant sees the other's uncommitted rows and the other tenant's call commits or rolls back on its own. (3) **Queue:** joined calls run one at a time on the ambient connection. A call made while another runs waits in a per-ambient FIFO queue (replacing R1-D-48's refusal of a concurrent sibling); a call made from inside a running joined call runs at once, so a nested call never queues behind its own caller; the ambient callback's own statements and units also wait while a joined call runs (`PgTx.turn`), so no statement runs under another call's savepoint or settings. A call or statement left behind by a joined call whose callback has settled is refused (`KernelGuardError`), as R1-D-92 refuses one after the ambient mutation ends. (4) **Errors:** a joined call that throws or fails in SQL rolls back to its savepoint, its caller's settings come back and the error reaches its caller; the ambient transaction stays usable. If the restore (or a joined read's rollback) itself fails, the ambient mutation is marked broken: queued calls and later statements are refused and it rolls back even when the caller caught the error. Files at most 32 MiB by default (64 MiB cap), at most 16 signatures. (3) **Coverage:** `coversWholeDocument` per signature; the document is `valid` only when every signature is valid and one covers the whole file, else `incremental_update_after_signature` (so B-LT and B-LTA files, which add a DSS or a document timestamp after the signature, are reported that way or as `invalid`). (4) **Trust:** `CCA_INDIA_TRUST` (`cca-india-trust.ts`, PEM with SHA-256 fingerprints checked at load); **every CA certificate on the path must be pinned** (an intermediate carried only in the PDF is not trusted); path ≤ 6; `cA`, `keyCertSign` when key usage is present, `pathLenConstraint`; an unknown critical extension fails the path (key usage, basic constraints, extended key usage and subject alternative name are the critical ones processed); names chain by exact DER bytes. **The pin set is empty:** cca.gov.in is not reachable from the build environment and no second-hand copy is pinned, so every chain is `chain_untrusted` until the owner supplies the certificates (#178). `customTrustStore` exists for tests and is reported as `trustStore: "custom"`. (5) **Signer:** found by issuer-and-serial or subject key identifier; ESS `signingCertificateV2`, when present, must hash to it; key usage required with `digitalSignature` or `nonRepudiation`; an extended key usage, when present, must include document signing, email protection, Adobe authentic documents, Microsoft document signing or any usage; signed attributes are required. (2) **One name rule** (`contracts/ports`): bullmq 6 refuses `:` in a queue name and in a custom job id (the scheduler id `cron-<job>`); pg-boss 12 accepts `^[\w.\-/]+$` for a queue, its dead-letter queue and a schedule key (the job name). The platform rule is the one the adapters already applied, a subset of that intersection: lower case, a letter first, no `/` or `:`; a queue name has no `.` (`<queue>.dlq` is reserved) and at most 63 characters, a job name at most 100. (3) **The relay** (`tenancy`): each row's delivery is its own unit inside the tenant's batch transaction: a failure is caught, counted on that row (`attempts + 1`) and the pass goes on; the delivered rows are marked dispatched in the same commit (a failed commit redelivers them, idempotent on the event id, the existing at-least-once contract). After `maxAttempts` failed attempts (constructor option, 1 to 100, default 5, as `int.queue.default_attempts`) the row is parked in the new `tenancy.outbox_parked` (`tenancy/0027`) with a fixed label (`queue_refused` for `IPB-PORT-003`, `queue_unavailable` for `IPB-PORT-002`, `delivery_failed` otherwise; never the error text) and its attempt count, and a `<schema>.outbox.park` ledger entry in the same transaction; the batch's `dispatch` entry gains `failed` and `parked` counts. A parked row stays undispatched in its outbox; the discovery read and the drain both leave it out, so a parked tenant costs no transaction or ledger entry per pass. `OutboxParking.list(ctx)` shows a tenant's parks; `requeue(ctx, schema, eventId)` closes the open park (`requeued_at`, `requeued_by`, once: a restrictive policy) as a ledgered `tenancy.outbox.requeue` mutation by the operator, and the relay retries the row with a fresh budget (counted from the attempts at the park). `outboxEventJob(event)` builds the job (`eventJobName` name; ids, full type and envelope in the data); the reference relay uses it. **Defaults taken (owner question #193):** (a) one central parking table rather than columns on every module's outbox (no module or product migration; the relay role gains insert and select of the park keys on that table under tenant RLS, and a platform-scope select so its discovery read skips parked ids; the kernel's relay action rule is unchanged, the park entry is written inside the `dispatch` transaction); (b) the per-row unit is a caught delivery inside the batch transaction, not one transaction per row, so the ledger keeps one entry per batch; (c) every failure reason gets the same budget (a refused job is not parked on its first attempt); (d) `requeueRoles` defaults to `ORG_OWNER` and `ORG_ADMIN`, persons only (no agent or service); (e) the stricter platform name rule is kept rather than widened to the libraries' intersection (capitals and `/`), so names stay identifiers. Idempotent; running it again refreshes the column grants, and `tenancy.refresh_ecosystem_inbox_jws_grants()` does so for every restricted inbox (a later migration that adds an inbox column runs it). The kernel's statement guard already refuses callback SQL that sets any `app.*`, so it has the trust of `app.tenant_id` (tested for `set_config` and `set local`). The break-glass preflight and the rate limiter set only `app.tenant_id` and never read the JWS, so they are unchanged. (4) **Definers** (allow-listed in the RLS lint's `DEFAULT_ALLOWED_DEFINERS`; `search_path = pg_catalog`; executable by app_rw and app_ro only): `tenancy.eco_inbox_jws_readable(schema)` (true when no role is registered for the inbox, else when `app.roles` holds one) and `tenancy.eco_inbox_jws(schema, source, event_id)` (refuses a non-reader with `42501` before any lookup, then returns the row's `jws` filtered explicitly on `app.tenant_id`, because the owner may bypass RLS; `null` for another tenant's or a missing row). The readers are therefore roles held **in the row's own tenant**: the product's security role reads a lender tenant's proofs only in a context of that tenant. The definers run as the migration identity, which must be able to read the product's inbox (true when one identity runs every migration, as `infrabyx-migrate` does); otherwise the read fails closed. (5) **`EcosystemInbox`** reads `jws` only through the definer (the duplicate re-read in `receive`, the replay check in `verified`, the handler's event in `drain`/`sweep`, fetched just before `handle`, and `list`), so its results are identical on an inbox that is not restricted. | 2026-11-27 | R1-D-294 | `[OWNER]` + `[ASSUMED – owner review]` **CVE-2026-124851 (zstd): R1-D-291's reasoning corrected, the runtime's zstd decode paths closed, and the waiver shortened to 2026-12-07 (LawDocsComply LDC-68, its SEC-ZSTD-01; owner, 27 Nov 2026 07:45 IST; threat model §3.194; guide §7fb; owner question #209).** (1) **Correction:** R1-D-291 said the finding was not reachable because Node.js links its own bundled zstd for `node:zlib`. That premise does not clear it. Node.js 24.22.1 and 24.22.3 bundle zstd **1.5.7** (`process.versions.zstd`, checked here on 24.22.1), inside the affected 1.5.1 to 1.5.7 range. body-parser 2.4.0 (Express 5.2.1, under `@nestjs/platform-express` 11.2.7) decodes any `Content-Encoding: zstd` request body with `zlib.createZstdDecompress()` before a guard runs (`lib/read.js`), and a client that reads back what it sent may recover up to 64 KiB of process memory per request (ComplyCl demonstrated it). Node's `fetch` (bundled undici 7.30.1) also offers `zstd` over https and decodes a zstd response whatever was offered (tested). R1-D-291's waiver of the Debian `libzstd1` package stands only because both paths are now closed in the code. (2) **Inbound:** `refuseZstdBodies` (and `refuseZstdBodiesWith({ productPrefix, typeBase })`) in a new `@infrabyx/connectors/content-coding`. It is connect/Express middleware: any `Content-Encoding` naming `zstd` or `x-zstd` (any case, any list position, repeated headers) gets 415 with an RFC 9457 problem: `IPB-SEC-010` (the code the governed egress already uses for an unsupported coding, so no new code), `reason: content_encoding`, the path only as `instance`, `Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, br` (RFC 9110 §15.5.16), `Connection: close`. The body is never read. gzip, deflate, br and identity pass. `apps/reference/api` registers it first, straight after `NestFactory.create` (Nest adds its parsers at `init`). A test counts `zlib.createZstdDecompress` calls (none) and sends a broken zstd body (415, not body-parser's 400), so it fails if the order changes. The scaffold copies `app.ts`, so new products have it. (3) **Outbound:** `refuseZstdFetch(fetchImpl?)` sends `Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, br` (replacing any caller's value, in the caller's header shape) and refuses a zstd response by cancelling its body unread (`RefusedContentCodingError`). `createEgress` (every REST adapter's outbound path) wraps its fetch, injected ones included, and maps the refusal to `IPB-SEC-010` without retry. OpenFGA's two direct `fetch` calls use it. Cerbos's client (`@cerbos/http`, global fetch) is built with the same `Accept-Encoding`. Consent's OH ledger, Vidhi's MCP client and the reference web app's API calls send the same `Accept-Encoding`. The governed egress and partner mTLS clients (`node:https`) already refuse every coding but identity, gzip, deflate and br. Unleash (minipass-fetch) never decodes zstd. AWS SDK, OTLP, Temporal (gRPC) and ssh2 do not decode response codings. The platform's own code never calls a zstd API (searched). **Residual, `[ASSUMED – owner review]` (#209):** undici builds its decoder from the response headers and pipes data into it at once, so a sender that ignores `Accept-Encoding` can still make the decoder start on the first bytes. Its output is cancelled unread and reaches no caller, store, log or sender, which is what the disclosure needs. A dispatcher-level refusal would close even that, but needs undici internals or a new dependency. (4) **Waiver:** `CVE-2026-124851` in `infra/docker/trivyignore.yaml` now expires **2026-12-07** (was 25 Dec), the date all four repositories share. Before then, move to a fixed Node.js or base image as soon as one exists; if none exists on 5 Dec, ask the owner. Checked at this session's start (27 Nov 2026, about 12:25 IST): no Node.js 24 release after 24.22.3 (10 Nov).
